page.layout: One page of text in a single column; running head at the top with the page number at its right; no marginal notes; no catchword or signature.

main_text.l: Regium est, bene facere, male audire, Il-
lud faciam modo, hoc feram libens. (Deo
gratias ago) patienter audire possum etiam
quæ mihi affingunt Inimici deterrima. Spe-
ro quoque me plus boni facturum, quam aut
merentur Ifti, aut cupiunt.
Olim (credo) manifestum fiet, eos qui
cætera mea Regna turbare cæperant, reos
esse magnam partem etiam horridi istius in
Hybernia cruoris, si non quâ primo fusi, at quâ
tardè repressi.
Quem certè (quicquid ipsi dicant vel
sentiant) non aliter accipio, quàm è venis
meis hauftum tantum sanguinis, cum ne-
mo prorsus, sat[?] scio, plus hâc effusione de-
bilitetur. Quanquam verò infariata[?] sit ho-
minum sævitia, spero Dei misericordiam
Iustitiæ Ipsius aliquando dicturam, sufficit, &
Civilium Bellorum Gladium in vaginam
suam recondi iussuram, cum misericors Il-
lius Iustitia non perniciem nostram velit, sed
Medicinam: ut sit scelerum diminutio, non
gentis excidium.

l.i: Misericordiis, quèus[?] Ego & Populus Meus fu-
mus valde abusi, necsut[?] unquam restituantur, me-
tas sub Religionis specie exercetur, quasi Chri-stians

page.notes: Running head and Greek title are set in Greek letters (ΕΙΚΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΚΗ); the scan shows them with Latin-looking capitals, transcribed as the Greek they spell. "infariata" (line 3 of the third paragraph) is uncertain; "sat" in "sat scio" is uncertain because the long s looks like f; "quèus" is doubtful (probably quibus); "necsut" is doubtful as printed. The last line of the page is cut off at the bottom edge, so the final word may be incomplete. Long s has been normalised to s throughout. The asterisk after "excidium" is an ornament and is not transcribed.
